name: Revenue share
mechanics: Investor provides capital in exchange for a fixed percentage of the company's ongoing gross revenues; payments flex with monthly revenue until a repayment cap is reached.
pros: Non-dilutive; founders retain full control (no equity given up).
cons: Often more expensive than bank debt; needs existing revenue.
evidence_quote: investors inject capital (sometimes called an advance) into a business in return for a fixed percentage of ongoing gross revenues
notes: Wikipedia calls the revenue percentage 'royalties'. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Milestone tranches
mechanics: Committed capital is released in staged portions ('tranches'), each unlocked when the company reaches agreed milestones, funding against progress to reduce risk.
pros: Lowers investor risk; disciplines spend against milestones.
cons: Funding uncertainty if milestones slip; admin overhead.
evidence_quote: is one of a number of related securities offered as part of the same transaction. In the financial sense of the word, each bond is a different slice of the deal's risk.
notes: Quote is the general structured-finance sense of 'tranche'; the venture 'milestone tranche' usage = staged release gated on milestones. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: SEALs
mechanics: Investor provides upfront capital and later receives a percentage of 'Founder Earnings' (salary + dividends + retained earnings) once a threshold is met, capped at a multiple; no equity, board seats, or fixed repayment schedule.
pioneered_by: Earnest Capital / Calm Company Fund (Tyler Tringas)
examples: Earnest Capital / Calm Company Fund portfolio
pros: Founder-aligned; no forced growth or exit; founders keep control.
cons: Niche; needs a path to founder earnings/profitability.
evidence_quote: The goal of a SEAL is to align the interests of investors and founders in a wide variety of outcomes, while giving founders full control of their business and keeping as much optionality as possible open for the business
notes: SEAL = Shared Earnings Agreement, created by Earnest Capital/Tyler Tringas (now Calm Company Fund). Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Royalty financing
mechanics: Capital repaid via a royalty - a percentage of revenue or sales - rather than equity or fixed debt; closely related to revenue-based financing.
cons: Can be costly; ties up a share of revenue.
evidence_quote: is a type of financial capital provided to growing businesses in which investors inject capital (sometimes called an advance) into a business in return for a fixed percentage of ongoing gross revenues (called royalties)
notes: Wikipedia redirects 'Royalty financing' -> 'Revenue-based financing'; the percentage is literally called 'royalties'. Classic royalty financing can also mean royalties on a specific product/IP - a distinct nuance pending a dedicated source. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Capped returns
mechanics: Investor returns are limited to a preset cap - typically a multiple of the original investment (commonly ~1.3x-3x); once the cap is repaid, the obligation ends.
pros: Predictable maximum cost to the company; defined (not unlimited) return.
cons: Caps investor upside (unattractive to power-law investors); company still pays the full cap.
evidence_quote: Usually, the returns to the investor continue until the initial capital amount, plus a multiple (also known as a cap) is repaid.
notes: Cap = a multiple of the investment (~1.3x-3x in RBF). The same 'capped return' idea underlies capped-return equity deals (e.g., Indie.vc/Calm) - dedicated source pending. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Shared earnings
mechanics: Repayment is a percentage of 'founder earnings' (profit available to founders) rather than gross revenue or equity; the family of structures underlying the SEAL.
pioneered_by: Earnest Capital / Calm Company Fund (Tyler Tringas)
pros: Aligns to profitability; founder-friendly; no forced exit.
cons: Only works once the company can pay founder earnings.
evidence_quote: The goal of a SEAL is to align the interests of investors and founders in a wide variety of outcomes, while giving founders full control of their business and keeping as much optionality as possible open for the business
notes: Shared earnings is the repayment mechanic underlying the SEAL (Earnest/Calm, Tyler Tringas); shares a source with the SEALs node. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Venture debt
mechanics: Debt financing for venture-backed companies from specialized banks or non-bank lenders to fund working capital or capex, complementing equity while minimizing dilution; lenders often take warrants.
examples: Providers incl. Hercules Capital, TriplePoint Capital, Comerica
pros: Less dilutive than equity; extends runway.
cons: Adds debt obligations; lender warrants give up some upside.
evidence_quote: Venture debt or venture lending is a type of debt financing provided to venture-backed companies by specialized banks or non-bank lenders to fund working capital or capital expenses
notes: Lenders typically take warrants for 5-20% of loan value (per source). Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: Comm. warrants
mechanics: A warrant gives the holder the right to buy stock at a fixed strike price before expiry; often attached to debt/financing as an equity 'sweetener'.
examples: Attached to venture debt and bonds as an equity kicker
pros: Lets lenders/investors share upside; lowers borrowing cost.
evidence_quote: a warrant is a security that entitles the holder to buy or sell stock, typically the stock of the issuing company, at a fixed price called the strike price
notes: Commonly attached to venture debt (5-20% of loan value). Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).

name: SAFE variants
mechanics: A SAFE gives an investor the right to future equity for capital paid now, without setting a share price at signing; converts at a later priced round/liquidity event, usually with a valuation cap and/or discount. Variants include pre-money and post-money SAFEs.
examples: Y Combinator standard SAFE; post-money SAFE
pros: Fast, low-cost, founder-friendly alternative to convertible debt.
cons: Stacked SAFEs can dilute founders more than expected.
evidence_quote: A simple agreement for future equity (SAFE) is an agreement between an investor and a company that provides rights to the investor for future equity in the company similar to a warrant, except without determining a specific price per share at the time of the initial investment.
notes: Created by Y Combinator (Carolynn Levy), late 2013, as an alternative to convertible notes; pre-money and post-money variants. Verified anchor (Ethan blueprint).
